extracted.intended_audience: applicants and agents entering the national phase under the PCT (international patent applicants and patent practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory/optional requirements for entering the national phase of a PCT international application before designated/elected Offices, including translations, copies, declarations, representation, priority restoration, amendments, and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical requirements for translation
rubrics_metrics.description: The translation of the international application and any copy of drawings must comply with the physical requirements prescribed by the designated Office; no designated Office may require compliance with form requirements different from or additional to those laid down in the PCT and the Regulations for filing international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the papers furnished comply with the physical requirements for international applications, they must be accepted by the designated Office. For details refer to International Phase paragraphs 5.177, 6.032 and 6.051.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of copies of the translation
rubrics_metrics.description: One copy of the translation is in principle sufficient for entering the national phase, but some designated Offices require two or more copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices that require more than one copy mention this in the National Chapter (Summary). If copies are missing, Offices will generally give the applicant an opportunity to furnish them once the national phase has started.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of the translation
rubrics_metrics.description: The translation furnished for entry into the national phase does not need to be certified by a public authority or sworn translator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if a designated Office reasonably doubts the accuracy of the translation, it may require the applicant to furnish a certification of the translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of the translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification means the translation must be accompanied by a statement signed by the applicant or translator that, to the best of the signatory’s knowledge, the translation is complete and faithful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only a few designated Offices require verification. For Offices that do, the National Chapter (Summary) indicates this and provides further details (including forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of the international application (whether required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under normal circumstances, designated Offices do not require the applicant to submit a copy of the international application; only a few do when the IB has not communicated a copy under Article 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Bureau communicates copies under Rule 93bis.1 and informs the applicant by Forms PCT/IB/308; upon receipt of those notices the applicant need not furnish a copy. National Chapters list Offices that require a copy and related details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy for early processing requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant makes an express request for early processing before the International Bureau has communicated the international application, the applicant must either furnish a copy of the international application (and any Article 19 amendments) to the designated Office at the time of the request or request the International Bureau to transmit a copy to the designated Office under Article 13(2)(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All other acts prescribed for entry to the national phase must also be performed when making such a request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of kinds of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing the request indicates the international application is for the grant of every kind of protection available by designation; if the applicant wants treatment as a different kind of protection (e.g., patent of addition, utility certificate, continuation), the applicant must indicate that choice to the designated Office when performing acts to enter the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Offices may require such indications at the time of performing the acts under Article 22/39, while others may allow indication or conversion later as provided by national law. National Chapters contain specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming of inventor for national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: If the name or address of the inventor(s) was not indicated in the request at filing, that information must be furnished to designated Offices at the time of entry into the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most Offices will invite the applicant to furnish missing inventor information if not provided on entry, but some will not; details are in the National Chapters. The indication of name/address is distinct from other inventor-related declarations considered 'special requirements'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of national forms
rubrics_metrics.description: No applicant may be required to use a national form to perform the acts prescribed for entry into the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many designated Offices keep national forms available and recommend their use. National Chapters list existing forms and annexes reproduce samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and timing of 'special requirements'
rubrics_metrics.description: Special requirements are national-law requirements (other than Article 22(1) acts) that designated Offices may require but cannot demand before the expiration of the time limit for entering the national phase; they may be complied with after entry into the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 51bis lists common special requirements and provides that the applicant must be given an opportunity to comply (usually by invitation with a time limit or by statutory time limit). National Chapters list special requirements per Office and indicate whether an invitation will be sent or a time limit applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents proving inventorship/right to file
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on national law, designated Offices may require documents relating to (i) identity of the inventor; (ii) applicant’s entitlement to apply or be granted a patent; (iii) proof of entitlement to claim priority when applicant differs or name changed; (iv) an oath or declaration of inventorship; (v) evidence regarding non‑prejudicial disclosures/exceptions to lack of novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Rule 4.17 declaration may obviate the need for such documents unless the Office reasonably doubts the declaration. Required documents must be sent to the designated Office (not the International Bureau). Annexes contain forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to comply with inventor/right-to-file requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Such requirements generally must be complied with within at least two months from the date of an invitation sent by the designated Office if not already complied with in the national phase entry time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some designated Offices have informed the IB that two months is incompatible with their national law; consult National Chapters for variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 4.17 declarations to simplify national processing
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may include declarations in Box No. VIII of the request form under Rule 4.17 concerning: (i) identity of inventor; (ii) entitlement to apply/be granted a patent; (iii) entitlement to claim priority; (iv) declaration of inventorship (USA only, must be signed); (v) non-prejudicial disclosures/exceptions to novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the request contains declarations under Rule 4.17(i)-(iv), a designated Office may not (except where it informed IB otherwise) require documents related to those subjects unless it reasonably doubts the declaration. For Rule 4.17(v) (non‑prejudicial disclosures), designated Offices are always entitled to require further documents or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation for national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Most designated Offices require non-resident applicants to be represented by an agent, while others require an address for service in the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Chapters indicate whether appointment of an agent or provision of an address for service is required. It is highly recommended to appoint an agent when performing acts to enter the national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of agent — form and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment of an agent must be made in a power of attorney signed by the applicant(s) and applies once the national phase has started.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model powers of attorney are in the National Chapter annexes and at WIPO’s PCT forms website. An address for service (where required) should be indicated at the time of performing the entry acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may act as agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Which persons may act as agent for the national phase is determined per designated Office and is provided in each National Chapter (Summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists with names/addresses of agents may be obtained from designated Offices (not from the International Bureau).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document submission timing and originals
rubrics_metrics.description: The priority document must be submitted during the international phase to the receiving Office or to the International Bureau, which makes it available to designated Offices; if submitted within the international phase time limit, no designated Office may require an original certified copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices may require a simple photocopy of the original priority document together with a translation (see below). See International Phase paragraph 5.070 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of the priority document
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated Office may require a translation of the priority document only where validity of the priority claim is relevant to patentability determination or to determine whether an incorporated element/part is completely contained in the priority document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If part of description/claims/drawings was incorporated by reference, the Office may require an indication where the part is contained in the translation of the priority document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive conditions of patentability in national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: The PCT leaves each Contracting State free to determine substantive conditions of patentability (e.g., what constitutes prior art); PCT does not change substantive national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because PCT prior art definitions are often as strict or stricter than national law, risk of unexpected prior art is reduced, but national law may require the applicant to furnish evidence in the national phase regarding substantive conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of errors in translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors in the translation of the international application may be rectified during the national phase before designated Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope of the translation may not exceed the scope of the international application in its original language. If translation scope is narrower, it may be broadened but not exceed original scope; if broader, the designated Office may limit scope accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of receiving Office decision to restore priority
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision by a receiving Office to restore the right of priority based on 'due care' will generally be effective in all designated Offices unless a designated Office submitted a notification of incompatibility; a restoration based on 'unintentionality' is effective only in designated States whose laws provide for restoration on that criterion (or more favorable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision by a receiving Office to refuse restoration can be reviewed by a designated Office unless it has submitted a notification of incompatibility under Rule 49ter.1(g). Review of a positive decision by a designated Office is limited to reasonable doubt that substantive requirements were complied with; purely formal grounds may not be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a request to restore priority directly with a designated Office
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to restore the right of priority can be filed directly with a designated Office once the applicant has entered the national phase before that Office, subject to incompatibility notifications by some Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices that notified incompatibility under Rule 49ter.2(h) will not accept such requests. Consult WIPO lists of incompatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to request restoration with a designated Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit is at least one month from the applicable time limit under Article 22 for entering the national phase, though designated Offices are free to apply longer time limits where national law permits; different start rules apply if express request under Article 23(2) was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the designated Office requires a declaration/evidence in support, it allows a reasonable time to furnish such documents. Refer to Rule 49ter.2(f) and National Chapters for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file a request to restore the right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must be submitted by way of a letter to the designated Office and, to be successful, must meet the listed requirements (priority claim present, international application filed within two months from expiration of the priority period, state reasons, pay any fee, and provide declaration/evidence if required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the priority claim was added after filing, it must have been added before the Rule 26bis.3(e) time limit. The statement of reasons should be drafted in light of the restoration criterion the applicant seeks (due care or unintentionality). Check National Chapter Annex I for fee requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for restoration of the right of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated Offices generally apply one or both of two criteria for restoration: (a) failure occurred in spite of due care required by the circumstances, or (b) failure was unintentional. Offices must apply at least one of these or a more favorable criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Office may apply both criteria if it wishes. The statement of reasons should match the criterion relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the statement of reasons for restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement should indicate the reasons for the failure to file within the priority period and contain all relevant facts and circumstances enabling the designated Office to determine whether the failure occurred despite due care or was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft the statement in light of the restoration criterion sought and be prepared to furnish supporting declarations or evidence if invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond to intended refusal of restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: If the designated Office intends to refuse the request for restoration of the priority claim, it must notify the applicant of its intention and give the applicant an opportunity to make observations within a reasonable time specified in the notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notification may be sent together with an invitation to file declarations or other evidence; applicants should use the opportunity to present supporting facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of incorporation by reference decisions by designated/elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated and elected Offices may, to a limited extent, review decisions by receiving Offices that allowed incorporation by reference; if they find failures (e.g., obligation to furnish priority document not complied with, missing statement of incorporation, missing translation, element not contained), they may treat the international application as if the filing date were the date on which the sheets containing the missing or correct element were submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before doing so, the Office must give the applicant the opportunity to make observations on the outcome, and the applicant may request that the missing part or correct element be disregarded. National notifications of incompatibility under Rule 20.8 may also affect handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of the international application in the national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are guaranteed an opportunity to amend claims, description and drawings before any designated Office in the national phase; designated and elected Offices must permit such amendments for at least one month from the time the applicant enters the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many Offices permit amendments at any time during national examination. Where examination must be specifically requested, requests to amend may only be made after entry into the national phase. National Chapters provide further indications and any exceptional time limits under Rules 52.1 and 78.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of obvious mistakes (rectification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obvious mistakes in the description, claims and drawings may normally be corrected before the designated Office; correction can be presented as an amendment provided the scope of the international application as originally filed is not broadened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated and elected Offices must generally process the international application 'as rectified' unless they already started processing before notification of rectification. An Office may disregard an authorized rectification if it finds it would not have authorized it; however, it must give the applicant an opportunity to make observations before disregarding. Conditions for rectification depend on national law and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review in the national phase of certain international-phase decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated Office may review certain decisions made in the international phase affecting the international application: (i) refusal to accord an international filing date by the receiving Office; (ii) declaration that the international application is considered withdrawn because of defects or non-payment; (iii) IB finding that the application is considered withdrawn because the record copy was not received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review consists of examining whether the receiving Office’s refusal/declaration or the IB’s finding was the result of an error or omission. To exercise review the applicant must request the IB to send documents and request each designated Office to review, give facts/evidence, pay national fee, and furnish translations where required; these actions must reach the authority within two months from notification of the unfavorable decision. Results may include treating the application as if the error/omission had not occurred or maintaining the effect under Article 24(2) even if no error is found. Applicants may request excusing of delays where relevant.
